title: Some late practice notes (these late practices are killing my workflow!): • Wanted to provide more detail on the final period of practice because I've never seen anything like it. They set up a 10-minute overtime period with the 1's against the 1's and the 2's against the 2's. The second-team offense got the ball first, presumably setting up the first-team offense with the chance to drive for the "win." It didn't exactly work out that way. Both offenses sputtered. The 2's went three-and-out on their first drive and Harbaugh then had long snapper Ben Mann, punter Jordan Stout and a punt returner (Calvin Austin) as the only players on the field. Stout boomed a punt 60 yards for a touchback. On the 1's first drive, Jaxson Dart hit Isaiah Likely for a 13-yard gain on a curl for their lone first down. Malachi Fields dropped a well-thrown back-shoulder fade to stall the drive. Stout then had a 41-yard punt to Xavier Gipson. The 2's got one first down on a 10-yard in route by Thomas Fidone. Stout then kicked a 56-yard touchback with Braxton Berrios back to return. A hold on the first play (a Cam Skattebo run off right tackle) killed the next drive. It looked like Abdul Carter and Darius Alexander combined for a sack on third-and-long. Stout then boomed a 61-yard punt to the other 20-yard line. The second-team offense operated the hurry-up after taking over at their own 20 with two minutes remaining. Isaiah Hodgins and Dalen Cambre had first-down catches before the offense faced fourth-and-3 from the opposing 47. Jameis Winston hit Cambre on a quick out for 3 yards to keep the drive alive. Three straight incompletions, including an Odell catch along the sideline that was ruled out of bounds and a PBU by Art Green, set up fourth-and-10 from the 44. It wasn't clear what the coaches were going to do, but Cam Skattebo and Isaiah Likely pleaded with the coaches to let Dominic Zvada to attempt a 62-yard field goal. With the wind at his back, Zvada drilled the kick with room to spare. • Tremaine Edmunds jumped a curl on the first play of practice and nearly had an interception. Two plays later he tipped pass while chasing Dart out of the pocket. Edmunds has really good ball skills for a LB. There have been a lot of tipped balls in camp from all the QBs, which signals it's an emphasis of the defense. • Korie Black mixed in with Deonte Banks and Colton Hood as a first-team corner. Huge opportunity upcoming for Black with so many corners injured. • After spending the first two weeks of camp almost exclusively on the third-team OL, Evan Neal has gotten some second-team reps at LG this week. It's now or never for the former first-round pick.

title: Hard to believe it’s been five years since Mark Cook (@markcook1970), longtime Bucs and @PewterReport beat writer, left us suddenly and unexpectedly at the age of 50. Seeing Mark live out his dream of covering the Bucs for over a decade was truly special. He did it with unrivaled enthusiasm and a flair all his own. You could feel this in every piece he wrote, every “What’s Cooking with Mark Cook” video he did, on every Pewter Report podcast and when he took the mic on 98.7 The Fan radio. But what I hold onto most: the way he made everyone around him feel a sense of belonging, and his care for others. Getting into this business (and staying there) can be rough. But Mark was always the first to extend his hand and introduce himself. I can remember so many times he’d stay late into the evenings at One Buc helping a young reporter with a notebook or giving an ear to someone who simply needed it. I was so excited for him when he began working as a teacher at Connecticut School of Broadcasting and honored when he asked a few of us to come speak to his class. Mark genuinely cared about the people around him and not just the surface-level things. He wanted to really know how you were doing and how your family was doing. He spoke proudly of his son Douglas and so lovingly of his partner @DaiseyWTSP. And he put together some legendary Thanksgiving BBQ celebrations. The Bucs honored him with a special video board tribute and reserved this seat for him, including his chef’s hat 🥺🥺🥺🥺🥺. @BruceArians called him a “dear friend and a hell of a professional. @MikeEvans13_ said, “We loved him in the locker room. I loved him.” @PFWAwriters Tampa chapter renamed our annual “Good Guy Award” in his honor. Thank you to @gregauman for so thoughtfully doing this. It’s presented to the player who is most helpful and cooperative with local media. We’ve gotten to a point where the guys now winning this award, like @TristanWirfs78, never had the chance to sit down and talk to him. Gosh he would have loved that. That saddens me, but it also gives me and others a chance to speak of how truly special he was, how much pride he took in this job and how he didn’t take a single moment on this earth for granted. His final good deed on this earth was that in lieu of flowers, his family requested donations be made to the @AriansFF to help foster children, a cause very dear to his heart.

title: Commanders just wrapped their joint practice with the Dolphins. Irresponsible amount of observations coming. 🏈 Miami is not going to be good. That's important to state before I comment any further about how lopsided in WSH's favor today's practice was. And it did feel lopsided at times. 🏈 Marco Rubio was there. So were Nats POBO Paul Toboni and manager Blake Butera. 🏈 Daniels looks great in the new offense. He looks smooth under center and he was awesome in play-action boot game today. 🏈 Diggs is a beast. He's a terrific route runner and he's going to help the Commanders a ton. He's just fun to watch run routes. Legit special in one-on-one drills (which are WR friendly), but that carried over to the team period. 🏈The first play of practice in the team period was a false start on WSH (Conerly I think). He had a rough rep in 1-on-1 vs Chop Robinson (designed to help the DL). He also got into it with a defender in the only 'skirmish' I saw all day. I like that feistiness from him. 🏈 The Commanders couldn't run the ball between the tackles much. In general, the one area I saw that looked like it needed lots of work was their interior OL play in run game. 🏈 One of my favorite plays was on a 2nd-and-6 from the 44. Daniels found Burks on an over route behind the linebackers on a play action shot. Beautifully layered throw. Looked like a throw you've seen in the Ben Johnson / Kevin O'Connell offenses for years. 🏈 Both kickers were strong today. They both went 6-for-6 and made kicks from 60 yards, their longest attempt of camp. Today's kicks were from 33, 38, 43, 48, 52, and 60. 🏈 Bill had a quiet day in terms of yards because there weren't holes but he ran hard. He also had a violent collision late in practice where he lowered his shoulders and helmet on the sideline instead of going out of bounds and delivered a blow. Many of his teammates came running down the sideline to celebrate with him. Terry McLaurin was very fired up. 🏈I only saw Daniels get sacked one time. I think there was another play that could have been a sack when he flushed the pocket to his right to extend a play. Pass pro was pretty solid but there was also a lot of booting him out of the pocket. 🏈Amik Robertson had a loud pass breakup on the outside and proceeded to talk trash to the entire Dolphins sideline. He was pointing at and shouting at several guys as he continued to play from the middle of the field. Funny moment. He's a super competitive, outspoken guy. I like watching him. 🏈Lawrence Cager has had a good camp. I think WSH has five tight ends that could all play in the league somewhere. Best position group they have IMO. 🏈 Daniels was surgical in a 2-minute drill at the end of practice. Looked like they set the clock at 30 seconds or so and had to move the rock. He went 4/5 with two completions to Diggs underneath. Threw a dime to Chig to move sticks for 8 yards as Okonkwo ran out of bounds.

🏈 Daniels looks great in the new offense. He looks smooth under center and he was awesome in play-action boot game today. 

🏈 Diggs is a beast. He's a terrific route runner and he's going to help the Commanders a ton. He's just fun to watch run routes. Legit special in one-on-one drills (which are WR friendly), but that carried over to the team period. 

🏈The first play of practice in the team period was a false start on WSH (Conerly I think). He had a rough rep in 1-on-1 vs Chop Robinson (designed to help the DL). He also got into it with a defender in the only 'skirmish' I saw all day. I like that feistiness from him. 

🏈 The Commanders couldn't run the ball between the tackles much. In general, the one area I saw that looked like it needed lots of work was their interior OL play in run game. 

🏈 One of my favorite plays was on a 2nd-and-6 from the 44. Daniels found Burks on an over route behind the linebackers on a play action shot. Beautifully layered throw. Looked like a throw you've seen in the Ben Johnson / Kevin O'Connell offenses for years. 

🏈 Both kickers were strong today. They both went 6-for-6 and made kicks from 60 yards, their longest attempt of camp. Today's kicks were from 33, 38, 43, 48, 52, and 60.

 🏈I only saw Daniels get sacked one time. I think there was another play that could have been a sack when he flushed the pocket to his right to extend a play. Pass pro was pretty solid but there was also a lot of booting him out of the pocket. 

🏈Amik Robertson had a loud pass breakup on the outside and proceeded to talk trash to the entire Dolphins sideline. He was pointing at and shouting at several guys as he continued to play from the middle of the field. Funny moment. He's a super competitive, outspoken guy. I like watching him.

title: The NFL needs to allow more color-on-color matchups. The primary reason for teams first adding white jerseys was so people could differentiate on black-&-white TVs. Account for the color-blind population (so no red-v.-green) but white should not be the jersey worn most often in any Broncos season. There's no reason why the Broncos shouldn't be able to wear orange when they play Pittsburgh or Las Vegas, for example. Or orange when the Chargers wear blue.

title: Broncos alternate uniform thoughts: A little surprised to not see all-white on Christmas like last year, even though it's a home game. Somewhat disappointed to have just two throwback games. League regulations limit teams to four "alternate" jersey games -- five for those with Rivalries uniforms -- so, they chose navy twice and throwbacks twice. Silly NFL rules. Need to change that to add at least one more so the recent trend of wearing throwbacks vs. divisional opponents could have been extended. Expect the Rams game will be all-navy (helmet, jersey, pants, socks), but hopefully the Bills navy game will see another white element to go with the helmet, either socks or pants. When they wore white helmets with navy jerseys, pants and socks in 2024 vs. Cleveland, it looked unbalanced.
